evidence.detail: Every Actor constructs and owns one rs/a/e instance; Actor delegates hit insertion/update directly to it, while the client reads its four active slots during overhead rendering.

The class owns exactly four active rs/a/f slots plus an overflow/replay CopyOnWriteArrayList, replaces expired slots using client-cycle timestamps, can clear all hit state, and exposes active-slot checks.
The same client loads hit-display assets from literal hitmarks/... paths and exposes the config key hitMarkStyle labelled "Hitsplats", making Hitmark the client-native noun for the managed records.

proposals.note: HitmarkManager describes the Actor-owned lifecycle/slot manager for the client's hitmark records; it is a semantic recovery name, not an original-identifier claim.

evidence.detail: The class is the object rendered from each Actor hit slot. Its two client-facing render paths select old/new hitmark sprite sets, position the mark above the Actor, and draw the numeric damage value.

Client resources used by this rendering path survive under literal names such as hitmarks/old/hit, hitmarks/old/crit, hitmarks/old/heal, hitmarks/old/poison, hitmarks/old/venom, hitmarks/new/block and hitmarks/new/hit N.
rs/a/e constructs rs/a/f from hit style/type, damage/value and auxiliary icon data, assigns display offsets/duration, and expires the record using the client cycle.

proposals.note: Hitmark follows the exact project resource terminology and the record's damage-display behavior; Hitsplat is intentionally not used because hitMark is the surviving client term.
